# LOADING PACKAGES. 
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(text = element_text(size = 15)))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# LOAD IN DATA.
```{r LOAD IN DATA}
# Create dataframe "data" which contains cleaned participant data without pure controls.
data <- read_csv('../Data/data_cleaned.csv') # Read csv data file.
```

# STANDARDIZE VARIABLES.
```{r STANDARDIZE VARIABLES}
# Standardize panas.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(panas = scale(panas))

# Standardize panas_pos.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(panas_pos = scale(panas_pos))

# Standardize panas_neg.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(panas_neg = scale(panas_neg))

# Standardize delta_ih.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(delta_ih = scale(delta_ih))

# Standardize affective_polarization.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(affective_polarization = scale(affective_polarization))

# Standardize third_order.
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(third_order = scale(third_order))
```

# FORMAT DATA.
```{r FORMAT DATA}
# Exclude participants who identify as "Pure Independent".
data <- data %>% 
  filter(pid7 != "Pure Independent") # Filter out (!=) participants who identify as "Pure Independent".

# Create indicator which classifies if a participant identifies as a Democrat (TRUE) or not (FALSE).
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(democrat_indicator = str_detect(pid7, "Democrat")) # If a participant identifies as a Democrat, the term "Democrat" will appear in pid7. If "Democrat" is detected in pid7, then assign a TRUE value. Otherwise, assign a FALSE value.
```

# RUN REGRESSIONS.
```{r RUN REGRESSIONS}
###############PANAS###############
# Run regression, saving as "panas_model".
panas_model <- lm(panas ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on panas.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
panas_model_summary <- tidy(panas_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
panas_model_statistics <- summary(panas_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.

###############PANAS POS###############
# Run regression, saving as "panas_pos_model".
panas_pos_model <- lm(panas_pos ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on panas_pos.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
panas_pos_model_summary <- tidy(panas_pos_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
panas_pos_model_statistics <- summary(panas_pos_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.

###############PANAS NEG###############
# Run regression, saving as "panas_neg_model".
panas_neg_model <- lm(panas_neg ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on panas_neg.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
panas_neg_model_summary <- tidy(panas_neg_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
panas_neg_model_statistics <- summary(panas_neg_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.

###############IH###############
# Run regression, saving as "ih_model".
ih_model <- lm(delta_ih ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on delta_ih.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
ih_model_summary <- tidy(ih_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
ih_model_statistics <- summary(ih_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.

###############AP###############
# Run regression, saving as "ap_model".
ap_model <- lm(affective_polarization ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on affective_polarization.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
ap_model_summary <- tidy(ap_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
ap_model_statistics <- summary(ap_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.

###############THIRD ORDER###############
# Run regression, saving as "third_order_model".
third_order_model <- lm(third_order ~ treatment * democrat_indicator, # Effect of treatment and political identity on third_order.
                      data = data) # Specify dataframe.

# Save two summaries of the regression model.
third_order_model_summary <- tidy(third_order_model) # Save the estimates, standard errors, and p-values.
third_order_model_statistics <- summary(third_order_model) # Save the r^2 values, F-statistics, etc.
```

# FORMAT REGRESSION RESULTS - ESTIMATE, STD.ERROR, P-VALUE.
```{r FORMAT REGRESSION RESULTS - ESTIMATE, STD.ERROR, P-VALUE}
###############ADD IN OUTCOME COLUMN###############

# Add a column "outcome" to panas_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("panas").
panas_model_summary$outcome <- "panas"

# Add a column "outcome" to panas_pos_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("panas_pos").
panas_pos_model_summary$outcome <- "panas_pos"

# Add a column "outcome" to panas_neg_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("panas_neg").
panas_neg_model_summary$outcome <- "panas_neg"

# Add a column "outcome" to ih_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("ih").
ih_model_summary$outcome <- "ih"

# Add a column "outcome" to ap_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("ap").
ap_model_summary$outcome <- "ap"

# Add a column "outcome" to third_order_model_summary which contains the variable used in the regression ("third_order").
third_order_model_summary$outcome <- "third_order"

###############BIND DATAFRAMES TOGETHER###############

# Bind the model summaries (estimates, standard errors, p-values) into one dataframe "summaries".
summaries <- rbind(panas_model_summary, panas_pos_model_summary, panas_neg_model_summary, ih_model_summary, ap_model_summary, third_order_model_summary)

###############FORMAT COLUMN VALUES###############

# Add significance stars based on p-value.
summaries <- summaries %>% 
  mutate(stars = case_when(p.value <= 0.001 ~ '***', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.05, then assign one star. 
                           p.value <= 0.01 ~ '**', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.01, then assign two stars. 
                           p.value <= 0.05 ~ '*', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.001, then assign three stars.
                          .default = ' '))

# Round estimates and add significance stars.
summaries <- summaries %>% 
  mutate(estimate = paste(round(estimate, 3), stars)) # Round estimates to three decimal places, and paste in significance stars.

# Round standard errors and add parentheses.
summaries <- summaries %>% 
  mutate(std.error = paste0("(", round(std.error, 3), ")")) # Round standard errors to three decimal places, and paste parentheses around the standard error values.

###############PLACE STANDARD ERROR VALUES BELOW CORRESPONDING ESTIMATES############### 

# Duplicate every row.
summaries <- summaries %>%
  tidyr::uncount(2, .id = "id") # Create two of every row, and label if a row is a 1st or 2nd copy in column "id".

# Add copy id to term column. This creates a unique marker for each row.
summaries$term <- paste(summaries$term, summaries$id) # Paste together term column and id column.

# Replace every other row in the estimate column with a blank. This ensures only one unique estimate per term category remains.
summaries$estimate[seq(2, nrow(summaries), by = 2)] <- '' # Starting at row 2, replace estimate value with ' '. Do this every other row (by = 2) until the end of summaries is reached.

# Replace every other row in the std.error column with a blank. This ensures only one unique estimate per term category remains.
summaries$std.error[seq(1, nrow(summaries), by = 2)] <- '' # Starting at row 1, replace estimate value with ' '. Do this every other row (by = 2) until the end of summaries is reached.

# Merge the estimate and std.error columns into a new column "combined_results".
summaries$combined_results <- paste(summaries$estimate, summaries$std.error)

# Reorganize the summaries dataframe.
summaries <- summaries %>% 
 pivot_wider(id_cols = c(term), names_from = outcome, values_from = c(combined_results)) # Identify observations using the column "term". The columns should be each outcome, and the values within the column should be taken from combined_results.

###############REORDER ROWS###############

# Reorder the rows of summaries, so that the rows containing the intercept estimates and standard errors are at the bottom of the dataframe.
summaries <- rbind(summaries[-c(1,2), ], summaries[c(1,2), ]) # Intercept estimate is the first row, and intercept standard error is the second row. Take the rows out of the dataframe (summaries[-c(1,2), ]), and bind it to the bottom of the dataframe (summaries[c(1,2), ]).

###############REFORMAT TERM COLUMN###############

# Replace every other value in the term column with a blank. This ensures only one unique value per term category remains.
summaries$term[seq(2, nrow(summaries), by = 2)] <- '' # Starting at row 2, replace estimate value with ' '. Do this every other row (by = 2) until the end of summaries is reached.

# Rename the remaining values in the term column so that they are more readable.
summaries$term[summaries$term =="treatmentTRUE 1"] <- "Treat" # Rename "treatmentTRUE 1" to "Treat".
summaries$term[summaries$term =="democrat_indicatorTRUE 1"] <- "Democrat" # Rename "democrat_indicatorTRUE 1" to "Democrat".
summaries$term[summaries$term =="treatmentTRUE:democrat_indicatorTRUE 1"] <- "Treat*Democrat" # Rename "treatmentTRUE:democrat_indicatorTRUE 1" to "Treat*Democrat".
summaries$term[summaries$term =="(Intercept) 1"] <- "Constant" # Rename "(Intercept) 1" to "Constant".
```

# FORMAT REGRESSION RESULTS - OBSERVATIONS, R^2, ADJUSTED R^2, RESID. STD. ERROR, F-STATISTIC.
```{r FORMAT REGRESSION RESULTS - OBSERVATIONS, R^2, ADJUSTED R^2, RESID. STD. ERROR, F-STATISTIC}
###############COMBINE OBSERVATIONS, R^2, ADJUSTED R^2... FOR EACH VARIABLE############### 

# For the variable panas, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "panas".
panas <- c(nrow(data), panas_model_statistics$r.squared, panas_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, panas_model_statistics$sigma, panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).

# For the variable panas_pos, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "panas_pos".
panas_pos <- c(nrow(data), panas_pos_model_statistics$r.squared, panas_pos_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, panas_pos_model_statistics$sigma, panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).
 
# For the variable panas_neg, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "panas_neg".
panas_neg <- c(nrow(data), panas_neg_model_statistics$r.squared, panas_neg_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, panas_neg_model_statistics$sigma, panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).

# For the variable ih, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "ih".
ih <- c(nrow(data), ih_model_statistics$r.squared, ih_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, ih_model_statistics$sigma, ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).

# For the variable ap, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "ap".
ap <- c(nrow(data), ap_model_statistics$r.squared, ap_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, ap_model_statistics$sigma, ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).

# For the variable third_order, combine number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value into a vector "third_order".
third_order <- c(nrow(data), third_order_model_statistics$r.squared, third_order_model_statistics$adj.r.squared, third_order_model_statistics$sigma, third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], pf(third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[1], third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)) # The F-statistic p-value can't be accessed directly from the model summary. Instead, compute the p-value using the F-statistic (third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[1]), and degrees of freedom (third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[2], third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[3]).

###############BIND VECTORS TOGETHER###############

# Create dataframe "statistics" which contains the number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, F-statistic, and F-statistic p-value for each outcome variable.
statistics <- as.data.frame(rbind(panas, panas_pos, panas_neg, ih, ap, third_order)) # Bind dataframes together.

###############FORMAT DATAFRAME###############

# Rename column "value.1", which is the 6th column, to "p.value".
colnames(statistics)[6] <- "p.value"

# Add significance stars based on p-value (p-values are contained in column value.1).
statistics <- statistics %>% 
  mutate(stars = case_when(p.value <= 0.001 ~ '***', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.001, then assign three stars.
                           p.value <= 0.01 ~ '**', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.01, then assign two stars.
                           p.value <= 0.05 ~ '*', # If the p-value is equal to or below 0.05, then assign one star. 
                          .default = ' '))

# Round all values to three decimal places.
statistics <- statistics %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3)) # For every value in the statistics dataframe that is numeric, round the value to three decimal places.

# Combine significance stars with F-statistics.
statistics <- statistics %>%
  mutate(value = paste(value, stars)) # F-statistics are contained in the column "value". Paste together F-statistics and significance stars.

# Delete significance stars and p-value columns.
statistics <- statistics %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(stars, p.value))

# Convert all columns in the statistics dataframe to character columns. This is necessary in order to later combine the summaries and statistics dataframes.
statistics <- statistics %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) # Convert all columns to character.

# Reorganize table, switching rows for columns and columns for rows.
statistics <- as.data.frame(t(statistics)) # The t() function is used to switch rows and columns.

# Create column "term" which contains the name of each statistic value in the dataframe.
statistics <- statistics %>%
  add_column(term = c("Observations", "R^2", "Adjusted R^2", "Resid. Std. Error (df=884)", "F Statistic (df = 3; 884)"))

###############NOTES ON RESIDUAL STANDARD ERROR AND F-STATISTIC DEGREES OF FREEDOM###############

# Note: the residual standard error degrees of freedom can be calculated using the code:
  panas_model_statistics$df[2]  
  panas_pos_model_statistics$df[2] 
  panas_neg_model_statistics$df[2] 
  ih_model_statistics$df[2] 
  ap_model_statistics$df[2] 
  third_order_model_statistics$df[2]
  
# Note: the F-statistic degrees of freedom can be calculated using the code:
  panas_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)]
  panas_pos_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)]
  panas_neg_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)] 
  ih_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)]
  ap_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)]
  third_order_model_statistics$fstatistic[c(2,3)]
```

# BIND REGRESSION RESULTS, FORMAT TABLE.
```{r BIND REGRESSION RESULTS, FORMAT TABLE}
# Create "table13" which contains the regression results contained in the summaries dataframe (estimates, standard errors, p-values) and the regression results contained in the statistics dataframe (number of observations, R^2 value, adjusted R^2 value, residual standard error, and F-statistic).
table13 <- rbind(summaries, statistics)

# Rename the columns to be more readable.
table13 <- table13 %>% 
  rename(
     ` ` = term, # Rename term as " ".
    `(PANAS)` = panas, # Rename panas as "(PANAS)".
    `(PANAS Pos)` = panas_pos, # Rename panas_pos as "(PANAS Pos)".
    `(PANAS Neg)` = panas_neg, # Rename panas_neg as "(PANAS Neg)".
    `(IH)` = ih, # Rename ih as "(IH)".
    `(AP)` = ap, # Rename ap as "(AP)".
    `(3rd order)` = third_order) # Rename third_order as "(3rd order)".

# Delete row names.
rownames(table13) <- NULL
```

# FINAL TABLE.
```{r FINAL TABLE}
print(table13)

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

kable(table13, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
      align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(table13) - 1)),
      caption = "Regression Results") %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"),
                font_size = 10, position = "center", full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, hline_after = FALSE) %>%  # Header row
  row_spec(1:nrow(table13), hline_after = FALSE)
```
